content.title: Pages, Layouts, and Shared UI
content.hook: A route needs page content. Real applications also need UI that stays around while the route changes.
content.context:
That is where layouts matter.

Imagine:

```text
Dashboard
├── Overview
├── Analytics
└── Settings
```

A dashboard shell might contain the navigation while the page area changes.
goals: Master Pages, Layouts, and Shared UI: Navigation does not always mean “throw away the whole interface and build it again.”

content.question:
A user moves from `/dashboard` to `/dashboard/settings`.

Which design best represents a shared dashboard shell?

options.text: Copy the sidebar into every page file.
Put the shared dashboard structure in a nested layout.
Put every route into one giant component.
Use a separate browser window for each page.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. Put the shared dashboard structure in a nested layout.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. Put the shared dashboard structure in a nested layout.

content.title: Why duplication hurts
content.text:
Suppose three pages each contain:

```tsx
<aside>...</aside>
```

The problem is not that the code is illegal.

The problem is that three copies create three places to maintain the same behavior.

A layout gives the shared UI one home.

content.title: Partial rendering
content.text:
When navigation occurs inside a routed application, the shared layout can persist while the page content changes.

That gives the learner an important mental model:

**Navigation does not always mean “throw away the whole interface and build it again.”**

content.question:
Design this route tree:

```text
app/
  dashboard/
    layout.tsx
    page.tsx
    reports/
      page.tsx
    settings/
      page.tsx
```

What belongs in the layout?

feedback.correct: Correct answer: A. The dashboard navigation and shell
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: A. The dashboard navigation and shell

content.title: Common mistake
content.text:
A learner often puts route-specific data into the shared layout simply because the layout is already there.

That can create an overly knowledgeable layout.

The better question is:

**Does this information truly belong to every child route?**

If not, keep it closer to the page that needs it.

content.question: Which is a good reason to use a nested layout?

options.text: To share route-level UI and structure without duplicating it
To force all state into one file

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. To share route-level UI and structure without duplicating it
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. To share route-level UI and structure without duplicating it

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: A good boundary gives shared UI a stable home without forcing unrelated concerns into it.
nextSteps: Take one existing multi-page interface and identify one piece of UI that should be shared through a layout. Explain why it belongs there and what should remain page-specific.

Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
